title: Open Rehearsal
intro: Text 1 is a social media post by a youth orchestra inviting the public to a rehearsal.

visual.text: Come and hear us get it wrong.
Free open rehearsal · Saturday, 3 pm · no ticket, no dress code, no shushing
A conductor in a T-shirt has stopped with her baton in the air, grinning. In front of her, teenage violinists in shorts and slippers are laughing at a mistake; one hides her face behind her bow.

A concert shows you the polished two hours. A rehearsal shows you everything that came before: the wrong notes, the restarts, the moment sixty players finally breathe together. This Saturday we are opening the doors. Sit anywhere. Walk around. Stand behind the drums if you dare.

visual.title: During the break
items: Try a cello, a trumpet or the timpani
Ask any player how long they have been learning
Find out how to join our beginners’ ensemble — no audition

visual.text: “I walked in thinking orchestras were for other people. I walked out having held a French horn.” — Wei Jie, 13, who joined last year
Eastwind Hall, Level 2. Children are welcome; noise is forgiven.

text2.intro: Text 2 is taken from a forum post by a teenager who went to one of the orchestra’s open rehearsals.
paragraphs: I only went because my cousin plays the violin and my aunt said the whole family had to show up. I expected two hours of sitting still and pretending to enjoy it. Instead, I watched the conductor stop everyone six times in the first ten minutes. The trumpets came in too early, then too late, and the whole hall groaned, laughed and tried again.

During the break, a bassoon player let me blow into her instrument. It made a sound like an angry goose, and nobody minded at all. That was when it hit me: these players were not born geniuses. They were ordinary teenagers who had simply kept practising. The next week, I put my name down for the beginners’ group.

questions.text: Look at Text 1. Which sentence best sums up what the post wants readers to take away?

options.label: A
options.text: The orchestra is looking for experienced players to fill its empty seats.

options.label: B
options.text: Anyone is welcome to watch real music being made, mistakes and all.

options.label: C
options.text: Concerts are a waste of money when rehearsals are free.

scheme.answer: Anyone is welcome to watch real music being made, mistakes and all.

questions.text: Look at the picture in Text 1. How does it support the headline ‘Come and hear us get it wrong.’?

scheme.answer: The young players are laughing at a mistake while the conductor grins, which shows that getting things wrong is a normal, relaxed part of a rehearsal and nothing to hide.
accept: The conductor and players are smiling after a mistake, so the picture shows the orchestra does not mind people seeing them get it wrong.
It shows the players in a relaxed mood laughing at their own error, which matches the headline’s promise that visitors will see mistakes.

seeds.text: The violinists are laughing at a mistake and the conductor is grinning, so it shows that making mistakes in rehearsal is normal and they are not ashamed of it, like the headline says.
Everyone in the picture is smiling even though someone just played wrongly, so it shows the orchestra is happy to let people watch them mess up.
It shows that the conductor is angry with the players for being careless.
The picture shows an orchestra practising their music.
A conductor in a T-shirt has stopped with her baton in the air, grinning.
